chunks: And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Basir who said:

I asked him about the one who is divorced (khula') by his father, who disowns him before the ruler, and regarding his inheritance and his debt/liability to whoever inherits him. He said, 'Ali (peace be upon him) said: "He belongs to the nearest of people to him."'

key_terms.أَقْرَبِ النَّاسِ إِلَيْهِ: The nearest of people to him
key_terms.الْمَخْلُوعُ: The one who is divorced (specifically khula' initiated by the father)
key_terms.يَتَبَرَّأُ: He disowns / declares himself free from

ai.seo_question: Who inherits a child who is divorced and disowned by his father?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the inheritance status of a child subjected to *Li'an* (oath of imprecation), where the father disowns the offspring before the judge. Citing Imam Ali (AS), it establishes that the child inherits from the nearest kin rather than the disowning father, highlighting the legal severance of the paternal bond in this specific context.
